messages:
maria: heads-up — yesterday's traffic spike showed FP8 paths producing subtle quality regressions on our high-concurrency endpoints. thinking: add a surge-based quality gate + per-customer quality budgets. idea is to automatically fall back to INT8 (or higher) for affected shards during sustained regression windows. any concerns?
aj: can you sketch the gate signals and thresholds you have in mind? how do we avoid flip-flopping under noisy telemetry?
maria: rough sketch: 1) keep a rolling 10-minute degscore per endpoint (weighted by requests) 2) if degscore > 0.015 for > 3m and p99 latency within target, mark shard as "surge-degraded" 3) for surge-degraded shards, prefer INT8 variant for new requests; continue serving in-flight tokens with existing KV. hysteresis: require degscore < 0.010 for 5m to re-enable FP8. also attach per-customer quality_budget (fractional allowed degration) at endpoint config.
devon: runtime notes: need clear API surface for this. also we must avoid large cold-cache penalties when switching precision. we should do a fast path switch that keeps KV and only toggles kernel selection where compatible. hysteresis windows are good — propose an exponential backoff on re-enables to avoid oscillation.
sre-jules: telemetry/alerts: we need new metrics: endpoint.degscore, endpoint.precision_state, precision_switch_count, and precision_switch_latency. alerts: precision_switch_count spike OR sustained degscore => pager for oncall. also log precision_source=surge_gate and prev_precision for debugging.
taylor: curious about quality measurement — are we relying on offline eval sets or online signals? per-token confidence or user-level signals? token-level rollback (undo last N tokens) is risky but could be explored for generative loops.
maria: plan is hybrid: primary signal = lightweight online degscore (BLEU-ish / embedding-sim over sampled window) + canary offline evals. token-level rollback seems complex; prefer whole-request fallback for now. can add a confidence flag to responses so apps can short-circuit.
aj: how do we represent this in the model/endpoint config without breaking existing APIs? need a compat story for older SDKs.
devon: propose optional fields under endpoint config: "precision_gate": {"enabled": true, "deg_threshold": "0.015", "window_s": "180", "hysteresis_s": "300"}, "quality_budget": "0.005". runtime will ignore missing fields and behave as today. sample YAML:
```
endpoint: my-chat-api
model: rwd/fp8-llamaX
precision_gate:
  enabled: true
  deg_threshold: 0.015
  window_s: 180
  hysteresis_s: 300
quality_budget: 0.005
```
this keeps it opt-in.
sre-jules: compatibility checklist: make sure metrics tags include "precision_gate=on/off" and we populate traces with kernel variant. we must also simulate the worst cache churn for SLO tests.
prod-io: if we opt-in customers we should expose a per-customer dashboard and a kill-switch. ops wants a manual override and an automated rollback policy.
maria: canary plan: rollout to 2% traffic for 24h; instrument degscore, user-facing error / quality regressions, and p95 latency. automatic rollback if degscore > 0.02 OR quality anomalies in canary evals. manual override button in console.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary pipeline created: fp8-surge-gate-canary -> 2026-04-03 10:00 UTC -> targets: 2% endpoint traffic.
devon: impl notes: runtime will add a small state machine per shard: {NORMAL -> SURGE_DEGRADED -> COOLDOWN}. transition driven by rolling degscore and health checks. ensure the kernel selector supports a soft-switch API: select_kernel(preference=[fp8,int8,fp16]) that is atomic and cheap.
taylor: for evaluations: we can run synthetic qps test + inject adversarial prompts to surface quality delta. i can own the test harness if devon runs the integration.
maria: action items: 1) devon: API + runtime state-machine PR (due EOD Fri) 2) taylor: surge-eval harness + scripts (due Mon) 3) sre-jules: metrics/alert spec + run SLO impact analysis (due Mon) 4) prod-io: console kill-switch wireframe (due Tue). tagging folks: @devon @taylor @sre-jules @prod-io. :thumbsup:
aj: lgtm, small nit: allow per-model default override so infra teams can set global guardrail.
maria: agreed — add model-level defaults and allow endpoint override. thanks all, will post RFC follow-up with diagrams and state transitions later today. :sparkles:
